title: Collisions: a crate lands on a floor

steps.text: Select **$root**, the top node of your scene.
steps.why: New nodes are added under whatever node is selected.

steps.text: Click **+**, search for `StaticBody2D`, and press **Create**. This will be the floor.
steps.why: A StaticBody2D never moves by itself, but other bodies bump into it — perfect for floors and walls.

steps.text: With **$floor** selected, add a `CollisionShape2D` as its child.
steps.why: A body has no size of its own. Its collision shape says what part of space it fills.

steps.text: In the Inspector, click **<empty>** next to **Shape** and choose **New RectangleShape2D**.
steps.why: A rectangle is the simplest shape, and a good fit for a flat floor.

steps.text: Click the new **RectangleShape2D** to open it, and make **Size** wide — for example x `600`, y `40`.
steps.why: The shape is still tiny. Making it wide gives the crate something to land on.

steps.text: Move **$floor** down the screen: select it and drag it in the 2D view, or set its **Position** (under Transform).
steps.why: Things fall downwards in Godot, so the floor needs to be below where the crate starts.

steps.text: Select **$root** again, then add a `RigidBody2D`. This will be the crate.
steps.why: A RigidBody2D is moved by physics: gravity pulls it down and it bounces off what it hits.

steps.text: With **$crate** selected, add a `CollisionShape2D` as its child.
steps.why: Just like the floor, the crate needs a shape before it can collide with anything.

steps.text: Give it a **New RectangleShape2D** in the Inspector, the same way as before.

steps.why: It needs some room to fall.

steps.text: Open the **Debug** menu in the top menu bar and tick **Visible Collision Shapes**, then press **Next**.
steps.why: Collision shapes are invisible in a running game. This setting draws them, so you can watch them work.

steps.text: Press **F6** (Play the currently edited scene) and watch the crate fall and land on the floor. Close the game window when you're done.
steps.why: F6 runs just this scene. Godot saves your work first.
